system_description.narrative_title: Escalation and global spillover of the Russia–Ukraine war
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative links renewed kinetic operations around Ukraine (strikes, drone attacks, local ceasefires) with widening geopolitical and economic knock‑on effects — maritime insecurity in the Black Sea, diplomatic rifts at the G20/UN, contested arms flows, and labour/action protests against weapons shipments. Framed as an open system, military actions, arms transfers, diplomatic pressure, energy and shipping disruptions, and information/cyber operations cross borders and feed back into each other: strikes provoke counterstrikes and political pressure, shipping losses spur policy and protest responses, and external actors (states, proxies, firms, institutions) alter incentives toward either escalation or temporary pauses.
system_description.scope: State and non‑state military actions and ceasefires tied to the Russia–Ukraine conflict; diplomatic negotiations and multilateral forum dynamics (G20, UN); arms transfers and defence industry activity; maritime security in the Black Sea and related shipping routes; labour and civil society responses to arms shipments; attendant humanitarian, energy and infrastructure impacts.
system_description.super_system: The global international order and security architecture (multipolar geopolitics, global trade and energy systems, and multilateral institutions).
adjacent_subsystems: Black Sea and global maritime trade/shipping
Global arms and defence industry / supply chains
Middle East & North Africa regional conflicts and proxy dynamics
Cyber, intelligence, and information warfare ecosystems

variables.name: Kinetic conflict intensity
variables.description: Measures the overall level of active military violence and kinetic operations (strikes, artillery, drone attacks, ground engagements) in the conflict system.

variables.name: Local ceasefire frequency
variables.description: Measures the rate at which temporary, localized ceasefires or pauses in hostilities are declared across frontline areas.

variables.name: Arms transfer volume
variables.description: Measures the flow rate and aggregate quantity of weapons, munitions, and military equipment being transferred between actors and into the conflict zone.

variables.name: Defence production capacity
variables.description: Measures the available industrial capacity and inventories that can be mobilized to produce military materiel and sustain supply to combatants.

variables.name: Maritime security risk
variables.description: Measures the likelihood and severity of hostile incidents affecting maritime routes and assets in adjacent sea regions.

variables.name: Shipping disruption rate
variables.description: Measures the frequency and intensity of interruptions to commercial shipping movements (delays, route changes, sinkings, interdictions) in affected sea lanes.

variables.name: Maritime insurance costs
variables.description: Measures prevailing risk premiums and insurance price levels for vessels and cargo operating in contested maritime areas.

variables.name: Diplomatic cohesion level
variables.description: Measures the degree of agreement and coordinated policy action among diplomatic actors within relevant multilateral and forum settings.

variables.name: Signalling and rhetoric level
variables.description: Measures the intensity and frequency of public signalling, threats, warnings, and diplomatic rhetoric emitted by actors in relation to the conflict.

variables.name: Cyber and information operation rate
variables.description: Measures the tempo and scale of cyber operations, information campaigns, and related digital influence activities targeting the conflict and its audience.

variables.name: Energy disruption level
variables.description: Measures the degree to which energy production, transit, and supply chains are interrupted or constrained as a result of the conflict and countermeasures.

variables.name: Humanitarian needs level
variables.description: Measures the aggregate scale of civilian displacement, unmet aid requirements, and essential service shortfalls caused by the conflict.

variables.name: Labour and protest intensity
variables.description: Measures the frequency and scale of strikes, labour actions, and civil-society protests that respond to or affect the arms flows and wartime logistics.

variables.name: Financial risk premium
variables.description: Measures the additional cost of capital, market volatility, and risk spreads attributable to geopolitical spillovers from the conflict.

variables.name: Ceasefire durability
variables.description: Measures the average persistence and resilience of ceasefires once established, including likelihood of relapse into hostilities.

variables.name: Escalation incentives balance
variables.description: Measures the net balance of political, military and economic incentives that push actors toward escalation versus incentives for restraint or de‑escalation.

catalysts.title: Global dockworkers strike over arms shipments
catalysts.description: Widespread port strikes targeting arms shipments continue or expand, disrupting logistics and commercial flows at dozens of global ports.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Dockworkers at more than 100 ports to strike against arms shipments' and 'Dockworkers at more than 100 ports worldwide strike against arms shipments'.

catalysts.title: Delivery process for approved Patriot interceptors
catalysts.description: Following US approval of a $2.1bn Patriot sale, transfer and integration processes will likely unfold, altering battlefield air-defence capabilities.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US approves $2.1 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine' implies imminent arms deliveries and capability changes.

catalysts.title: Negotiations and interest in limited Black Sea ceasefire
catalysts.description: Growing diplomatic interest in a limited Black Sea ceasefire to allow humanitarian and commercial shipments could produce short-term pauses or constraints.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US sees growing interest in limited ceasefire in Black Sea' and 'Poland calls for rapid ceasefire in Black Sea to allow food shipments'.

catalysts.title: Renewed strikes on energy and infrastructure
catalysts.description: Cycles of strikes and counter-strikes against energy and critical infrastructure (refineries, grids, transport hubs) are likely to continue, raising disruptions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Ukraine Hits Russian Oil Refinery, Ending Pause' and 'Russian strikes cut power to thousands'.

catalysts.title: Escalation of maritime drone and vessel attacks
catalysts.description: Drone strikes and maritime attacks on commercial vessels and convoys in the Black Sea and adjacent waters may increase, worsening shipping hazards.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Greek container ship sinks after drone attack' and 'Black Sea is now the world’s deadliest shipping route'.

catalysts.title: Rising military-technical ties with North Korea
catalysts.description: Reports of North Korean weapons testing, labour links and offers of assistance suggest growing military-technical and personnel ties with Russia.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'North Korea fires ballistic missiles' and 'North Korean labour advertised online to Russian factories'.

catalysts.title: Rifts at G20 and UN forums affecting coordination
catalysts.description: Ongoing disagreements at G20 and UN meetings over Ukraine and other conflicts will likely continue to reduce coordinated diplomatic action.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Rifts over wars in Ukraine, Middle East loom over G20' and 'G20 foreign ministers skip photo-op amid objections over Russia'.

catalysts.title: Looming Ukraine funding crunch and loan approvals
catalysts.description: EU and allied funding frictions and delayed loans may constrain Kyiv's procurement and humanitarian budgets, affecting operations and needs.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'EU pressures allies over looming Ukraine funding crunch' and 'EU Commission sets up framework for EU countries to approve remaining Ukraine loan by 2027'.

catalysts.title: Local ceasefires and evacuations around Oleshky
catalysts.description: Rare local ceasefires to allow evacuations in Oleshky may recur and could prompt temporary humanitarian relief and negotiations.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Russia observe rare Ukraine ceasefire to allow evacuations' and 'Aid convoy sets off for Russian-held town of Oleshky'.
